title: Franck Migone
text:
I work at the intersection of official statistics, public policy, and data science. Since 2021, I have worked at Côte d’Ivoire’s National Agency of Statistics (ANSTAT), where I serve as Deputy Director for Methodological Innovation and Head of DataLaB, ANSTAT’s data innovation lab.
My work explores how artificial intelligence, big data, and modern survey methods can improve economic measurement and public decision-making. I am particularly interested in labor markets, poverty, and economic development in Côte d’Ivoire and West Africa.

title: Franck Migone
text:
Current focus

Economic measurement: labor markets, poverty, education, and household welfare.
Statistical innovation: AI, satellite imagery, big data, and survey methods.
Knowledge sharing: teaching econometrics and sampling, and writing about economics and data.

title: Research
text: My research focuses on labor markets, poverty, education, and the use of new data sources for economic measurement.

title: Research
section: Job Quality and Poverty in Developing Countries: Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire
text:
Job Quality and Poverty in Developing Countries: Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire
Working paper · Read the paper
Using the 2018 Harmonized Survey of Household Living Conditions, this study examines how the quality of jobs held by household members relates to household poverty. The results suggest that better employment conditions—particularly women’s access to high-quality jobs—can reduce poverty risk.

title: Research
section: The Causal Impact of Armed Conflict on Education Outcomes in Mali
text:
The Causal Impact of Armed Conflict on Education Outcomes in Mali
With Josias Sadia
Working paper · Read the paper
Using difference-in-differences and propensity score matching, this study analyzes the effects of Mali’s prolonged crises on educational attainment. It finds a decline of 1.13 to 1.97 years of education among generations who were of school age during the conflict.

title: Research
section: Exposure to Violence and Academic Performance Among Adolescents in Côte d’Ivoire
text:
Exposure to Violence and Academic Performance Among Adolescents in Côte d’Ivoire
With Sekongo Coulibaly
Working paper · Read the paper
Using the 2018 Violence Against Children Survey, this paper studies academic outcomes among children aged 13 to 18. Exposure to violence is associated with greater risks of grade repetition and school dropout, underlining the need to connect education policy with child-protection measures.

title: Research
section: Estimating Poverty with Satellite Imagery in Developing Countries: Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire
text:
Estimating Poverty with Satellite Imagery in Developing Countries: Evidence from Côte d’Ivoire
With Kone Kinin Mamadou
Working paper · Read the paper
This study combines Sentinel-2 imagery, transfer learning, and household survey data to estimate poverty between survey waves. The preferred model closely reproduces the observed national poverty rates for 2018 and 2021, illustrating how satellite data can complement traditional welfare monitoring.
